However, the Emmys' "In Memoriam" segment bypassed the Walker, Texas Ranger star, drawing phantasmal applause in criticism.

Loretta was known for martial arts action films, but he also entered the television hall of fame for his role as lawman Cordell Walker in Walker, Texas Ranger. The show aired from 1993 to 2001.

Loretta passed away in March this year at the age of 86, just days after the Oscars ceremony, and likewise missed being honoured at that event.

However, for many viewers, his cowboy swagger in Walker, Texas Ranger may be more familiar.

Robert Redford and Catherine O'Hara, among other industry heavyweights, were properly included in the Emmys' farewell segment.

According to Deadline, others omitted by the Emmys (the version broadcast by NBC) were Nicholas Brendon of Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Patrick Muldoon of Melrose Place, and game show host Jaye P. Morgan.

All of the above are listed on the Emmys' "In Memoriam" webpage, but require considerable scrolling to find them. A Television Academy spokesperson also added that there is a "more comprehensive video" separately on the website.

The spokesperson said via email: "The tribute segment is only a few minutes long, and there are always limitations on how many people can be mentioned during the live broadcast."
